summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for acute-on-chronic left hip pain. He presented with worsening pain, chills, and elevated inflammatory markers, raising concern for septic arthritis. Imaging showed no fracture, and joint aspiration revealed no infection on gram stain or culture, supporting a diagnosis of left hip synovitis. He was treated with IV methylprednisolone and a fluoroscopic-guided steroid injection into the left hip, with subsequent improvement in pain and mobility. An MRI showed stable chronic sacroiliitis and worsening degenerative disc disease. His asthma and sleep apnea were managed with home medications and CPAP. He was discharged home ambulatory with a pain regimen, follow-up plans with rheumatology, and instructions to monitor for signs of infection.
